$doc: Vyomi capability registry — CloudWatch (metrics, alarms, dashboards) + CloudWatch Logs. See s3.json for the contract.

aws.cloudwatch.metrics.title: Metrics (PutMetricData, ListMetrics, GetMetricStatistics, GetMetricData incl. metric math)

aws.cloudwatch.alarms.metric.title: Metric alarms (create, evaluate on every PutMetricData, state + history)
limitations: Static threshold alarms and anomaly-detection-band alarms (see aws.cloudwatch.anomaly-detection) are both evaluated live.

SNS, Lambda (aws.cloudwatch.alarms.actions.lambda) and EC2 (aws.cloudwatch.alarms.actions.ec2) alarm actions really fire; Auto Scaling actions are not offered — see aws.cloudwatch.alarms.actions.compute.

aws.cloudwatch.alarms.composite.title: Composite alarms (AlarmRule grammar over child alarm states)

aws.cloudwatch.alarms.actions.compute.title: Auto Scaling alarm action
limitations: Auto Scaling alarm actions are not offered — Vyomi has no Auto Scaling group to act on. EC2 alarm actions are real — see aws.cloudwatch.alarms.actions.ec2.

aws.cloudwatch.alarms.actions.ec2.title: EC2 alarm action
limitations: Stop/Terminate/Reboot really change the state of the instance named by the alarm's own InstanceId dimension, through the same EC2 instance lifecycle (vpc_core.py) the EC2 console uses.
Recover isn't offered — AWS's underlying hardware-recovery automation has no equivalent in Vyomi.
If the alarm's metric carries no InstanceId dimension, the action is recorded as failed, the same as a real misconfigured EC2 alarm action.

aws.cloudwatch.alarms.actions.lambda.title: Lambda alarm action
limitations: The invocation is fire-and-forget, the same as a real CloudWatch alarm action: Vyomi does not surface the function's return value or errors back onto the alarm's history.

aws.cloudwatch.anomaly-detection.title: Anomaly detection bands
limitations: The band is a simple mean ± N standard-deviations model trained from the metric's own history (not AWS's ML model), so it won't learn seasonality or periodic spikes.
A SINGLE_METRIC detector trains (PENDING_TRAINING → TRAINED) once it has seen 10 datapoints; METRIC_MATH detectors stay PENDING_TRAINING.

aws.cloudwatch.dashboards.title: Custom dashboards (create, add widgets, save, delete)

aws.cloudwatch.dashboards.automatic.title: Automatic dashboards
limitations: Per-service automatic dashboards are an AWS-curated view over service metrics; Vyomi does not generate them.

aws.cloudwatch.metrics.multi-source-quer.title: Multi source query, cross-account Options and Source selection
limitations: Vyomi simulates a single account/region, so cross-account/cross-region metric source selection has nothing to select.

aws.cloudwatch.logs.groups.title: Log groups (create, retention, log class, KMS association, deletion protection, tags)

aws.cloudwatch.logs.subscription-filters.title: Subscription filters
limitations: Lambda and Kinesis destinations really receive the gzip+base64 `awslogs` envelope (a real invoke / PutRecord); a Firehose destination has no backing core and is kept as a delivery counter only.

aws.cloudwatch.logs.insights.title: Logs Insights queries (Logs Insights QL)
limitations: Supported: fields/display, filter (=, !=, >, <, >=, <=, like), sort, limit, pattern, stats count(*) [by field | by bin(duration)]. Only count() aggregation and OpenSearch PPL/SQL query languages are not offered.

aws.cloudwatch.logs.patterns-visualizati.title: Logs Insights Patterns and Visualization tabs
limitations: Patterns are mined with a simple tokenizer (numbers/hex/UUIDs masked to <*>, grouped, counted) — AWS's own clustering model may group lines differently.
Visualization only renders the result of a stats-by-bin() query (a bar list), not the full Logs Insights chart types (line/stacked area/pie).

aws.cloudwatch.logs.live-tail.title: Live Tail
limitations: Vyomi polls FilterLogEvents on an interval instead of the real bidirectional Live Tail streaming protocol, so new events can take a few seconds to appear.

aws.cloudwatch.logs.data-sources.title: Log management Data sources tab
limitations: Vended log sources (data source onboarding across accounts/services) are not modeled.

aws.cloudwatch.logs.data-protection.title: Log group data protection (sensitive data masking)
limitations: 8 managed data identifiers are recognized (EmailAddress, CreditCardNumber, Ssn-US, AwsSecretKey, AwsAccessKey, PhoneNumber-US, IpAddress, Url) — AWS's full managed identifier catalog (100+, with locale variants) is not offered.

Masking is enforced at ingestion (PutLogEvents permanently replaces the match with asterisks, as AWS does); Audit-only findings are counted on the log group but not forwarded to a findings destination (CloudTrail/Security Hub/S3).

aws.cloudwatch.logs.field-indexes.title: Log group field indexes
limitations: A field index is stored and returned exactly as AWS defines it (a cost/performance hint, not a correctness filter) — Vyomi's Logs Insights already scans every field, so indexing a field doesn't change query results or make the query faster, just like on AWS it doesn't change results, only cost.

aws.cloudwatch.logs.transformer.title: Log group transformer
limitations: 4 processors are run for real at ingestion (parseJSON, addKeys, deleteKeys, renameKeys), restructuring the stored event exactly as AWS does. AWS's other processors (grok, csv, splitString, substituteString, dateTimeConverter, type converters, …) are rejected by PutTransformer — not silently accepted.

aws.cloudwatch.logs.contributor-insights.title: Log group Contributor Insights rules
limitations: Only LogFormat JSON is scanned; CLF/W3C log formats are accepted and stored by PutInsightRule but GetInsightRuleReport finds no contributors for them.
Filters only support the In / NotIn operators (exact-value membership); AWS's other operators (IsPresent, StartsWith, …) are not evaluated.
The report is computed over the whole requested window as one bucket, not broken down per-Period like AWS's time series.
